subject: Hosted -> Dedicated migration: sizing validation & cutover plan
messages:
From: Alex Li <alex@euswitch.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@euswitch.com
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Hosted -> Dedicated migration kickoff: sizing inputs

Hi Ben / Marissa,

Thanks again for the call this morning. We want to formalize the sizing validation and cutover timeline for moving our production traffic from Redwood Hosted to a Dedicated pool. A few specifics to help your sizing:

- Current peak TPS observed: ~18 rps (sustained bursts to 35 rps for ~2 minutes)
- Avg tokens per request: 220 input / 160 output
- 95th latency target after migration: < 220ms P95 (from user edge to response token emission)
- We use streaming responses and KV-cache warm-up matters for our prompt flows (many conversations re-use prefixes)
- Expected go-live business date window: earliest Apr 6, latest Apr 20 (procurement has a 2-week review)

Procurement asks for an initial SOW and a recommended GPU configuration + estimated monthly committed capacity and cost bands. Can you also confirm a cutover blackout window and a dry-run rehearsal?

Attached is a 72-hour representative traffic sample (will send full file via separate email if helpful).

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Li
Head of Platform
Euswitch

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Li <alex@euswitch.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 13:26:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Hosted -> Dedicated migration kickoff: sizing inputs

Alex — thanks for the clear numbers and the sample. Looping in Engineering (Karthik) and Customer Success (Neha) to validate assumptions and lay out a rehearsal/cutover timetable.

High-level proposal from us (will refine after Karthik reviews the traffic):
- Preliminary Dedicated pool: 8x H100 or equivalent (we can show cost/latency delta vs 16x A100)
- Autoscaling headroom to hit burst 35 rps without queuing (short spikes handled by burst capacity policy)
- Preflight: controlled traffic replay + smoke test (1 full weekday, target week starting Mar 20)
- Dry run (full cutover rehearsal): weekend dry-run Mar 25-26 (non-prod routing + rollback rehearsal)
- Proposed cutover window: 02:00–04:00 UTC (2-hour blackout window) on Apr 10 (final date flexible pending procurement)

To keep the timeline realistic for procurement, we can ship an SOW draft by Mar 20 and a final sign-off/DocuSign run the week after. Can you confirm procurement's absolute latest start date and whether they need SOC2 artifacts attached to the SOW?

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Alex Li <alex@euswitch.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 08:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Hosted -> Dedicated migration kickoff: sizing inputs

Thanks for the data, Alex — the sample was helpful. A few technical notes and constraints from infra: 

1) Sizing estimate (ballpark, subject to full replay):
   - H100 footprint: 8 GPUs estimated (conservative) for target P95 < 220ms with batching tuned for 220/160 token mix and streaming on
   - A100 alt: 16x A100 required to hit similar P95, with ~1.6x higher infra cost in our current pricing bands

2) KV-cache warm-up: if customers have long tail (many unique prefixes), initial QPS can see 10–15% higher cost until cache reaches steady-state. We recommend a warm-up replay during preflight and a KV-prime step before the dry run.

3) Batching and concurrency: we'll propose batch size cap of 32 tokens/batch and a latency-aware batching policy (keeps tail low). For the 35 rps short bursts, we rely on burst pool (elastic overcommit for 20 minutes) — this requires a brief rate-limiter increase during the dry-run window.

4) Acceptance criteria for go/no-go:
   - P95 latency <= 240ms in rehearsal with identical traffic mix
   - No request-level error rate spike > 0.5%
   - Successful rollback under 10 minutes from traffic switch

I've attached the preflight checklist I use for these migrations. Ops will need a 48h lead to commission requested GPU pool size.

—Karthik
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
(attachment: preflight_checklist.xlsx)

From: Alex Li <alex@euswitch.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@euswitch.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 11:37:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Hosted -> Dedicated migration kickoff: sizing inputs

Thanks Karthik — that aligns with our internal estimates. Procurement confirms the earliest sign-off path is Apr 3 but they need the SOW and a copy of SOC2 + data flow diagram attached. They also asked for a 2-week lead time for finance to approve the committed capacity.

We attached the 72-hour traffic sample for the replay as promised (Euswitch_traffic_sample.json). One note: during business hours our traffic shows a geometric tail — there are many short conversations with repeated prefixes which should help caching, but we do see periodic spikes from a batch ingestion job around 03:30 UTC.

Please add the SOC2 artifact to the SOW and share a draft by Mar 20 so Procurement can start review.

Alex

Alex / team — attaching the SOW draft (SOW_v1.docx) and SOC2 pointer for procurement. Below is the agreed acceptance & cutover timeline we discussed; please confirm and I will push the DocuSign envelope.

Plan summary:
- Mar 20–22: Preflight traffic replay + KV-prime (engineering-led)
- Mar 25 (weekend): Dry run rehearsal (non-prod routing + failover exercises)
- Mar 27–28: Ops commission GPUs and do final smoke tests in dedicated staging
- Apr 03: Target earliest sign-off (procurement must finish by Apr 03 to hit Apr 10 cutover)
- Apr 10, 02:00–04:00 UTC: Proposed production cutover window (final confirmation after procurement)

Acceptance gates (go/no-go):
- Rehearsal P95 latency <= 240ms with production-like traffic
- Error rate < 0.5% during dry run
- Successful rollback tested within 10 minutes in rehearsal
